The study focused on the impact of invasive species on the biodiversity of the Kruger National Park.
The results showed that the presence of invasive species significantly reduced the number of indigenous species in the park.
The study also investigated the potential for these invasive species to spread to other areas.
The findings of the study can be used to inform conservation efforts and to develop strategies to mitigate the negative impacts of invasive species.

samples.src: Reproductive Hormones Imbalance, Germ Cell Apoptosis, Abnormal Sperm Morphophenotypes and Ultrastructural Changes in Testis of African Giant Rats (Cricetomys gambianus, Waterhouse, 1840) Exposed to Sodium Metavanadate Intoxication

samples.src: Environmental exposure to vanadium has been on the increase in recent time.
samples.ref: Go ba gona ga banadiamo go tikologo go oketšegile mo nakong ye e sa tšwago go feta.
samples.hyp: This is due to the increased use of vanadium in the production of steel and other alloys. The main sources of vanadium exposure are industrial activities, such. as the production of steel, the combustion of fossil fuels, and the use of vanadium-containing products.

samples.src: This metal is a known toxicant.
samples.ref: Metale wo o tsebja bjalo ka mpholo.
samples.hyp: Exposure to this metal can cause serious health problems, including damage to the nervous system, liver, and kidneys. The most common symptoms are nausea, vomiting, and abdominal pain. In severe cases, exposure can lead to death.

samples.src: The current study was conducted to investigate the reproductive toxicity of sodium metavanadate (SMV) in male African giant rats.
samples.ref: Dinyakišišo tše di dirilwe ka nepo ya go nyakišiša go ikoketša ga mpholo wa sodium metavanadate (SMV) go magotlomagolo a dipholwana a Afrika.
samples.hyp: The study aimed to determine the effects of SMV on sperm production, sperm motility, and sperm morphology in these animals.

samples.src: Administration of SMV was done intraperitoneally daily for 14 consecutive days at a dosage of 3mg/kg body weight.
samples.ref: Go di fa SMV go dirilwe ka dithong tša ka mpeng letšatši le lengwe le le lengwe mo matšatšing a go latelana a 14 ka selekanyo sa 3 mg/kg go boima bja mmele.

samples.src: Sterile water was administered to the control group.
samples.ref: Meetse a go seterelaeswa a tšhetšwe go sehlopha seo se laolwago.
samples.hyp: The control group consisted of 20 female mice. The purpose of this study was to determine whether the extract from the plant could reduce the growth of cancer cells.

samples.src: We analyzed serum reproductive hormones, sperm reserve and quality as well as testicular ultrastructural changes following SMV treatment.
samples.ref: Re ile ra sekaseka dihomoune tša go ikoketša tša seramo, tekano ya disepeme le boleng bja tšona ga mmogo le diphetogo tša sebopegotlaleletšo ka morago ga go a fa SMV.
samples.hyp:
```
Re ile ra nyakiša dihormone tša bokgophi tša seramo, tšhelete ya disemara le boleng, le go feta fao, diphetogo tša ultrastructure tša testise ka morago ga thibelo ya SMV.
```

samples.src: Our results showed SMV exposed AGR group had statistically increased progesterone but decreased testosterone, FSH and LH concentrations.
samples.ref: Dipoelo tša rena di laeditše gore ge SMV e filwe sehlopha sa AGR e oketša phrotšesteroune kudu eupša ya fokotša bontši bja thestosteroune, FSH le bja LH.

samples.src: Also, SMV treated group had statistically decreased sperm motility and mass activity with increased percentage of abnormal morphophenotypes of spermatozoa and upregulation of P53 immunopositive cell.
samples.ref: Gape, sehlopha seo se filwego SMV se bile le phokotšego ya go hwa ga disepeme le go gola ga boima bja mmele fao go bilego le persente ye e pketšegago ya mehutapopego ye e sego ya tlwaelega ya tlhamego ya disepeme le ya taologodimo ya disele tša imunophosethifi ya P53.

samples.src: Ultrastructural study revealed vocuolation of germ and Sertoli cells, cytoplasmic and nucleus; and mitochondrial swelling and vacuolations were also observed.
samples.ref: Dinyakišišo ka ga tlhamego ya disele di utollotše tlhamego ya dibakhule tša ditwatši le ga disele tša Sertoli tša saethopholasemo le tša nyutlelease; le go kokomoga ga maethokhontriale le tlkhamego ya dibakhule le yona e ile ya bonwa.

samples.src: There was severe disintegration of the seminiferous tubules, atrophy and degeneration of myeloid cells and apoptosis of the Leydig, Sertoli and germ cells.
samples.ref: Go bile le go hwelela kudu ga ditšhupu tša go sepetša disepeme, tshenyego le go hwelela ga disele tša maeloete le go hwa ga disele tša Leydig, Sertoli le tša ditwatši.

samples.src: In conclusion, intraperitoneal SMV exposure exerts severe adverse effects on some serum reproductive hormones, reduction of sperm reserve and quality, apoptosis and degenerative changes of the Leydig, Sertoli and germ cells which can lead to infertility.
samples.ref: Ge re fetša, go fa magotlo SMV ka dithong tša ka teng go tšweletša diabe tše mpe kudu go dihomoune tše dingwe tša tšweletšo ya seramo, go phokotšo ya poloko ya disepeme le go hwa ga disele le diphetogo tša go hwelela ga disele tša Leydig, Sertoli le tša ditwatši gomme se se ka feletša ka go hloka pelego.

samples.src: Researchers say metal found in polluted air makes rats infertile
samples.ref: Banyakišiši ba bolela gore metale wo o hweditšwego ka moyeng wo o šilafaditšwego o dira gore magotlo a palelwe ke go ikoketša

samples.src: Researchers found that vanadium, a type of metal, damages rats’ cells and their ability to create offspring (fertility).
samples.ref: Banyakišiši ba hweditše gore banadiamo, e lego mohuta wa metale, o senya disele tša magotlo le go kgona ga tšona go tšweletša magotlwana (go ikoketša).
samples.hyp: They also found that vanadium can cause inflammation and affect the development of the brain.

samples.src: Because this metal is also toxic to humans, they suggest more research to find out if the metal, which is increasingly found in our environment due to pollution, might have similar negative effects on human health.
samples.ref: Ka gobane metale wo le o na o na le mpholo go batho, ba šišinya gore go dirwe dinyakišišo tše dingwe ge tseba ge eba metale wo, wo gantši o hwetšwago tikologong ya rena ka lebaka la tšhilafatšo, o ka ba le diabe tše di swanago tše mpe go maphelo a batho.

samples.src: Even though vanadium is a metal, it can enter the air in tiny amounts when fossil fuels, like oil and coal, are burned.
samples.ref: Le ge e le gore banadiamo ke metale, o ka tsena moyeng ka ditekano tše nnyane kudu ge dibešwa tša fosilo tša go swana le makhura le malahla, a tšhungwa.

samples.src: As the world uses more of these fuel sources, the amount of vanadium pollution increases.
samples.ref: Ka ge lefase le šomiša bontši bja methopo ye ya dibešwa, tekano ya tšhilafatšo ka banadiamo e a oketšega.

samples.src: We already know that people exposed to it can suffer from health problems like anaemia, dry throats and eyes, and chest pains.
samples.ref: Re šetše re tseba gore batho bao e ba fetelago ba ka ba le mathata a maphgelo a go swana le go fela madi, megolo le mahlo tše di omeletšego, le dihlabi tša maswafong.

samples.src: Recently, scientists have also become interested in the effects that vanadium could have on fertility.
samples.ref: Mo nakong ye e sa tšwago go feta, bašomi ba tša mahlale le bona ba ile ba ba le kgahlego go diabe tšeo banadiamo e ka bago le tšona go tša pelego.

samples.src: They’ve started to study these effects in rats, which are often used in the laboratory because of their similarity to humans.
samples.ref: Ba ile ba thoma go nyakišiša ka ga diabe tše go magotlo, ao gantši a šomišwago ka laporathoring ka lebaka la go swana ga ona le batho.

samples.src: In this study, the scientists were interested in the effects of vanadium on a common type of rat found in West Africa, called the African Giant Rat.
samples.ref: Ka mo dinyakišišong tše, bašomi ba tša mahlale ba bile le kgahlego go diabe tša banadiamo go mohuta wo o swanago wa magotlo ao a hwetšwago ka Borwa bja Afrtika ao a bitšwago Magotlomagolo a Afrika.

samples.src: They wanted to understand how vanadium changes male rat reproductive systems, specifically their sperm, hormones, and the cells of their testicles.
samples.ref: Ba be ba nyaka go kwešiša ka fao banadiamo e fetošago tshepedišo ya go ikoketša ga magotlo a dipholwana, kudukudu go disepeme tša ona, go dihomoune, le go disele tša maretšana a tšona.

samples.src: The researchers injected 6 male rats with vanadium once a day, for 14 days.
samples.ref: Banyakišiši ba hlabetše magotlo a dipholwana a 6 ka banadiamo gatee ka letšatši, mo matšatšing a 14.
samples.hyp: The vanadium concentration in the injected rats' blood was measured. The results showed that vanadium caused a significant increase in the concentration of lead in the rats' blood.

samples.src: At the same time, they injected another 6 rats with water as a “control” experiment.
samples.ref: Ka yona nako yeo, ba ile ba hlabela magotlo a mangwe a 6 ka meetse bjalo ka tekolo ya “taolo”.

samples.src: Because water would be unlikely to affect the rats, the researchers could be sure that any changes they saw in the first six rats were the result of the vanadium injections.
samples.ref: Ka gobane meetse ga go na le klgonagalo ya gore a ka ama magotlo, banyakišiši ba be ba kgona go ba le bonnete bja gore diphetogo dife goba dife tše ba di bonego go magotlo a tshela a mathomo e bile dipoelo tša go hlabelwa ka banadiamo.

samples.src: After 14 days, they checked if the amount of hormones, like testosterone, had changed, and they examined their testicles and counted their sperm.
samples.ref: Ka morago ga matšatši a 14, ba ile ba lekola ge eba tekano ya dihomoune, tša go swana le thestosteroune, e fetogile, gomme ba ile ba hlahloba maretšana a tšona le go bala disepele tša ona.

samples.src: Using a technique called Transmission Electron Microscopy (TEM), they were able to see any changes that occurred in the testicles in detail, down to the level of individual cells.
samples.ref: Ka go šomišwa mokgwa wo o bitšwago Maekheroskoupu wa Phetošetšo ya Dielektrone (TEM), ba ile ba kgona go bona diphetogo tše di diregilego ka go maretšana ka botlalo, go ya fase maemong a disele ka botšona.

samples.src: The researchers found that the rats injected with vanadium had very low levels of testosterone, and other hormones important for fertility.
samples.ref: Banyakišiši ba hweditše gore magotlo ao a hlabetšwego ka banadiamo a bile le maemo a fase kudu a tšweletšo ya thestosteroune, le ya dihomoune tše dingwe tše bohlokwa tša pelego.
samples.hyp: This could be due to vanadium interfering with the production of these hormones.

samples.src: Vanadium-injected rats also had a lot less sperm, and their sperm was less healthy.
samples.ref: Magotlo ao a hlabetšwego ka banadiamo le ona a bile le disepeme tše nnyane, gomme disepeme tša ona di be se tša phela gabotse.

samples.src: The researchers saw, for example, that some of the rats’ sperm was headless or had a bent tail, and that it didn’t move as much as sperm from the rats injected with water.
samples.ref: Banyakišiši ba bone, go fa mohlala, gore tše dingwe tša disepeme tša magotlo di be di hloka dihlogo goba di na le mesela ya go kgopama, le gore a be a sa sepele kudu go swana le disepeme le tša magotlo ao a hlabetšwego ka meetse.

samples.src: Because sperm are the sex cells of male organisms, used to fertilise eggs in females, these changes would make it more difficult for the rats to successfully breed.
samples.ref: Ka ge disepeme e le disele tša thobalano tša dipehdinyana tša ditona, tšeo di šomišwago go nontšha mae a ditshadi, diphetogo tše di ka dira gore go be boima kudu gore magotlo a ikoketše ka katlego.

samples.src: Lastly, the researchers found that some of the cells from the rats’ testicles were badly damaged or even destroyed by vanadium.
samples.ref: Sa mafelelo, banyakišiši ba ile ba utolla gore tše dingwe tša disele tša maretšana a magotlo di be di senyegile kudu goba di sentšwe ke banadiamo.

samples.src: The researchers said that the changes they found could eventually cause complete infertility.
samples.ref: Banyakišiši ba boletše gore diphetogo tšeo ba di hweditšego mafelelong di ka baka go palelwa ke go ikoketša ka botlalo.

samples.src: They noted that since animals exposed to vanadium and other pollution in the environment may be unable to reproduce, they could possibly go extinct because of these effects.

samples.src: Cultural Use of Homegarden Plants in an Indigenous Community in North West Ethiopia
samples.ref: Tšhomišo ya Setšo ya Dimela tša Dirapana tša ka Gae go Setšhaba seo se phelago sekgale ka Leboa Bodikela bja Ethiopia

samples.src: The floristic composition of homegardens in Northwest Ethiopia in general, and the Gozamin district in particular, has received little research attention.
samples.ref: Tshedimošo ka ga dimela go dirapana tša ka gae ka Leboabodikela bja Ethiopia ka kakaretšo, le distriki ya Gozamin kudukudu, ga se ya fiwa šedi ye e lekanetšego ya dinyakišišo.

samples.src: The purpose of this research is to better understand the floristic composition and cultural significance of homegardens.
samples.ref: Morero wa dinyakišišo tše ke go kwešiša bokaone tshedimošo ka ga dimela le bohlokwa bja bja dirapana tša ka gae go setšo.

samples.src: Stratified random sampling procedure was used based on agroecological variation in selected kebeles.
samples.ref: Go šomišitšwe tshepedišo ya go sampola bakgathatema ka go ba arola ka dihlopha go lebeletšwe dipharologantšho tša temo le ekholotši go dikebele tše di kgethilwego.

samples.src: The homegarden data were collected by dividing the homegarden into four quadrats, the first quadrat stretched from the farmer’s home to 10m, the second quadrat from10m to 20m, the third quadrat from 20m to 30m and the fourth quadrat from 30m to 40m horizontally using farmer’s house as reference depending on the size of the garden.
samples.ref: Datha ya dirapana tša ka gae e kgobokeditšwe ka go arola dirapana tša ka gae ka dikwaterate tše nne, kwaterate ya mathomo e goga go tloga legaeng la molemi go fihla go 10m, kwaterate ya bobedi e tloga go 10m go fihla go 20m, kwaterate ya boraro e tloga go 20m go fihla go 30m gomme kwaterate ya bone e tloga go 30m go fihla go 40m ka go rapama go šomišwa ngwako wa molemi bjalo ka boikgakollo go lebeletšwe bogolo bja tšhengwana.

samples.src: A semi-structured interview was carried out to document the informant’s knowledge on plant species.
samples.ref: Go swerwe dipoledišano tše di beakantšwego gannyane go ngwala fase tsebo ya mokgathatema ka ga mehuta ya dimela.

samples.src: A total of 238 culturally important plant species from 81 families were identified.
samples.ref: Palomoka ya mehuta ya dimela tše bohlokwa go setšo tše 238 go tšwa magorong a 81 e hlaotšwe.

samples.src: Of these 39% were herbs,29% shrubs, 6% were climbers.
samples.ref: Godimo ga 39% tše e be e le mešunkwane, 29% mehlahla, 6% e be e le merarane.
samples.hyp: The remaining 26% were trees.

samples.src: Perennials made up the largest part of cultivated species (83%), whereas annuals made up the rest (17%).
samples.ref: Dibjalo tše di phelago go feta ngwaga di bopile karolo ye kgolokgolo ya mehuta ye e bjetšwego (83%), mola dimela tše di bjalwago ngwaga ka ngwaga ka moka di bopile (17%).

samples.src: The Poaceae family had the foremost species, with 22, taken after by the Fabaceae, which had 21, and the Asteraceae which had 15.
samples.ref: Legoro la Poaceae le bile le mehuta ya pelepele, ka palo ya 22, gomme ya latelwa ke Fabaceae, yeo e bilego le 21, le Asteraceae ye e bilego le 15.

samples.src: From these recorded plants,140 (58.6%) were species utilized for environmental uses, 84 (35%) food crops, 83 (34.7%) medicinal plant species, 39 (16.3%) fodder species, 57 (23.8%) material use plants, 60 (25%) fuel wood species, 50(21%) social use plants and 1 (0.4%) poisonous.
samples.ref: Go tšwa go dimela tše di begilwego, 140 (58.6%) e bile mehuta ye e šomišetšwago merero ya tša tikologo, 84 (35%) ya merogo ya go jewa, 83 (34.7%) ya mehuta ya dimela tša dihlare tša kalafo, 39 (16.3%) ya ba mehuta ya furu, 57 (23.8%) ya ba dimela tša tšweletša didirišwa, 60 (25%) ya ba mehuta ya dikgong tša go gotša mollo, 50 (21%) ya ba dimela tša go šomišwa ka gae le 1 (0.4%) ya ba tša mpholo.

samples.src: The direct matrix ranking revealed that Cordia Africana was found a versatile culturally important plant in the area which was also extremely threatened, followed by Ficus sur.
samples.ref: Tlhopho ya matrikse wa thwii e utollotše gore go hweditšwe gore Cordia Africana ke semela se bohlokwa mererong ya setšo ye bohlokwa ka tikologong, seo le sona se bego se le kotsing ye kgolo ya go nyamelela, sa latelwa ke Ficus sur.

samples.src: Cordia africana highest use-value was for Building and the list value was for medicinal.
samples.ref: Mohola o mogolo kudu wa tšhomišo ya Cordia Africana mo Meagong gomme boleng bja fasefase e be e le go tšweletšo ya dihlare tša kalafo.

samples.src: The Sorensen similarity index for 64 percent of the locations investigated was less than 0.5.
samples.ref: Intekse ya tshwano ya Sorensen ya diphesente tše 64 tša mafelo ao a nyakišišwago e be e le ka fase ga 0.5.
samples.hyp: This indicates that the microbial communities in these locations are very different from each other.

samples.src: The result showed that homegardens are multi-functional, long-term production systems.
samples.ref: Dipoelo di bontšhitše gore dirapana tša ka gae di šomišetšwa mabaka a go fapafapana, a mananeo a tšweletšo a paka ye telele.
samples.hyp: They provide food, medicine, and other resources for the community. They also contribute to biodiversity conservation.

samples.src: Food security and biodiversity conservation are continuously supported by tribal populations cultural knowledge connected with their homegardens.
samples.ref: Polokego ya dijo le pabalelo ya mehutaphedi di thekgwa go tšwela pele ke tsebo ya setšo ya ditšhaba tše di bušwago ke magoši ye e sepelelanago le diratswana tša bona tša ka magaeng.

samples.src: The less similarity/high species diversity in the area between kebeles indicated that there was high species diversity this was due to different range of agroecological conditions among kebeles.
samples.ref: Go swana gannyane ga mehuta ya dimela ka tikologong magareng ga dikebele e laeditše gore go be go na le pharologantšho ya godimo ya dimela, se se hlotšwe ke mehuta ye e fapafapanego ya maemo a temo le ekholotši magareng ga dikebele.

samples.src: Ethiopian gardens support food security and conservation
samples.ref: Dirapana tša Ethiopia di thekga tšweletšo ya dijo le pabalelo
samples.hyp: of biodiversity.

samples.src: Researchers say many Ethiopians grow food, decorative plants, medicinal plants and plants for animal feed, shade or fencing in their gardens.
samples.ref: Banyakišiši ba bolela gore bontši bja badudi ba Ethiopia ba bjala dimela tša dijo, dimela tša go kgabiša, dimela tša go dira dihlare le dimela tša go fepa diphoofolo, meriti goba go aga legora la diratswana tša bona.

samples.src: They analysed these gardens to see how important they are for ensuring food security and to help conserve the environment.
samples.ref: Ba sekasekile dirapana tše go bona ka moo di lego bohlokwa go kgonthiša tšweletšo ya dijo le go thuša go babalela tikologo.

samples.src: Communities around the world keep gardens for food, to make money and for other cultural purposes.
samples.ref: Badudi go lefaseng ka bophara ba itirela dirapana go tšweletša dijo, go dira tšhelete le merero ye mengwe ya setšo.

samples.src: Gardens also protect important plants that are often absent or disappearing in other areas.
samples.ref: Dirapana di šireletša le dimela tše bohlokwa tšeo gantši di sa hwetšagalego goba di nyamelelago ka ditikologong tše dingwe.

samples.src: In Ethiopia, not much research has been done on what exactly communities grow in their gardens.
samples.ref: Go la Ethiopia, ga se gwa dirwa dinyakišišo tše ntši mabapi le seo badudi ba tlogago ba se bjala ka dirapaneng tša bona.

samples.src: In this study, the researchers wanted to investigate the plants that people in Gozamin district, North West Ethiopia, grew in their gardens and what they used it for.
samples.ref: Ka dinyakišišong tše, banyakišiši ba be ba nyaka go nyakišišiša dimela tšeo badudi ba distriki ya Gozamin, Leboa Bodikela la Ethiopia, ba di lemilego ka dirapaneng tša bona le gore ba be ba di šomišetša eng.

samples.src: They identified and counted plants in 357 gardens in the area.
samples.ref: Ba hlaotše le go bala dimela ka dirapaneng tše 357 ka tikologong.
samples.hyp: They also collected soil samples from these gardens to analyze the presence of heavy metals.

samples.src: They also interviewed the community on what they use the plants for.
samples.ref: Ba swere le dipoledišano le badudi mabapi le gore ba šomišetša dimela mabaka afe.
samples.hyp: They found that the plants are used for medicinal purposes, for food, and for building materials.

samples.src: The researchers found that all the gardens in Gozamin were less than a hectare in size.
samples.ref: Banyakišiši ba hweditše le gore diratswana ka moka go la Gozamin di be di fetwa ke hekthara e tee ka bogolo.

samples.src: They collected and identified 238 different plants.
samples.ref: Ba kgobokeditše le go hlaola dimela tša go fapafapana tše 238.
samples.hyp: Of these, 158 were trees, 57 were shrubs, and 23 were herbs. The study also found that the area is home to a variety of animals, including mammals, birds, reptiles, and amphibians.

samples.src: Most (83%) of the plants were cultivated throughout the year, and only a few (17%) were seasonal.
samples.ref: Bontši (83%) bja dimela di be di bjalwa ngwaga ka moka, ke fela (17%) tše di bego di bjalwa go ya ka dihla.

samples.src: Their results showed that the community used plants for food, medicine, building, fodder (animal feed), and other cultural uses.
samples.ref: Dipoelo tša bona di bontšhitše gore badudi ba be ba šomiša dimela go tšweletša dijo, dihlare, furu (dijo tša diruiwa), le mabaka a mangwe a setšo.

samples.src: Most plants served more than one purpose.
samples.ref: Bontši bja dimela di be di na le mehola ya go feta o tee.

samples.src: For example, the Northern large-leaved tree could be used for medicine, decorating, fodder, shade, fencing and other cultural uses.
samples.ref: Mohlala, mohlare wa mahlare a magolo wa ka tikologong ya Leboa o be o ka šomišetšwa dihlare, go kgabiša, furu, morithi, go aga legora le mešomo ye mengwe ya setšo.

samples.src: Over half (59%) of the plants were used for environmental purposes such as fencing, hedges, shade and decorating.
samples.ref: Go feta seripagare (59%) sa dimela di šomišetšwe merero ya tša tikologo go swana le go aga legora, morithi le go kgabiša.

samples.src: The researchers said this helped to protect the environment.
samples.ref: Banyakišiši ba boletše gore se se thušitše go šireletša tikologo.
samples.hyp: They also said that the use of this method can help to reduce the amount of waste produced by factories.

samples.src: Fencing plants also helped to safeguard farm produce.
samples.ref: Dimela tša go aga legora di thušitše le go šireletša ditšweletšwa tša polaseng.

samples.src: Slightly over a third (35%) of the plants were harvested for food, such as fruit, vegetables, cereals and spices.
samples.ref: Kelo ya ka godingwana sa teetharong (35%) ya dimela tše di bego di bjalelwa go tšweletša dijo, bjalo ka dienywa, merogo, diserele le disepaese.
samples.hyp: The remaining plants were used for other purposes, such as medicine, construction, and fuel.

samples.src: They however said the gardens in the area mainly provided fruits.
samples.ref: Le ge go le bjalo, ba boletše gore dirapana ka tikologong di be di tšweletša dienywa kudu.

samples.src: The researchers said 35% of the plants were used as traditional medicine for human and animal wellbeing, while 21% were used for rituals and religious purposes, smoking, perfumes and baking.
samples.ref: Banyakišiši ba boletše gore 35% tša dimela di be di šomišwa bjalo ka dihlare tša setšo go thuša go alafa batho le diphoofolo, mola 21% di be di šomišetšwa merero ya ditšo le ya sedumedi, go kgoga motsoko, dinkgišabosana le go paka.

samples.src: Some plants (17%) were used as fodder to feed cattle, sheep, and donkeys.
samples.ref: Dimela tše dingwe (17%) di be di šomišwa bjalo ka furu ya go fepa dikgomo, dinku, le ditonki.
samples.hyp: Other plants (12%) were used for medicinal purposes, while the remaining plants (78%) were used for other purposes, such as building materials, firewood, and crafts.

samples.src: Others (24%) served as materials for building, making garden tools, roof thatching and making ropes.
samples.ref: Tše dingwe (24%) di šomišitšwe bjalo ka didirišwa tša go aga, go dira ditlabela tša ka diratswaneng, go rulela ka bjang le go loga dithapo.

samples.src: Since the majority of the rural populations reportedly used firewood, 25% of plants were used for that.

samples.src: The researchers said only one (0.4%) plant was mentioned for poisoning purposes.
samples.ref: Banyakišiši ba boletše gore ke fela semela se tee (0.4%) se go laeditšwego gore se šomišetšwa merero ya go tšhela mpholo.
samples.hyp: The plant was identified as belonging to the genus *Solanum*, which includes many poisonous plants.

samples.src: They also said the way plants were distributed in the area was influenced by the environment, what people liked to eat, as well as family financial status and business needs.

samples.src: The Wenka people also grew and supplied fruits and vegetables to the town market.

samples.ref: Sa mafelelo, banyakišiši ba boletše gore bontši bja balemi ba be ba rata go bjala dimela tše di bego di šomišetšwa mabaka a go fapafapana.
